lessons.title: Plan Project 42: weekly drift generator
lessons.build: Write the question and rule for `drift/README.md`. Type `make_week()`: a reference week of 5,000 orders (`distance_km`, `items`, `rush_hour` 50%), then 7 weeks of 1,500. From week 3 distance creeps +0.8 km a week; from week 5 the rush share is 75%. Items never change.
lessons.ask: Which feature should stay 'ok' all seven weeks, and why?
lessons.learn: Read 16.3: Goal, Skills used, Data, Architecture and the shop-crowd intuition. Re-read 10.2 on PSI.

lessons.title: PSI, KS and the seven-week table
lessons.build: Type `psi()` with quantile bins from the reference. Hand-check two bins: 50/50 against 70/30 gives 0.1695. Add `ks_2samp`. Print week, feature, PSI, KS, p and a status (below 0.1 ok, 0.1 to 0.25 watch, above 0.25 alert). Predict first when distance first alerts.
lessons.ask: Why must the bins come from the reference and not from the current data?
lessons.learn: Read 16.3 build steps 1, 2 and 4: PSI, the KS statistic, running seven weeks. Note the common pitfalls about empty bins.

lessons.title: Retrain rule and a text dashboard
lessons.build: Type `retrain_rule()` with persistence (2 weeks in a row). Check Practice Q6: `retrain_rule([{'a':0.3},{'a':0.1},{'a':0.3}])` is False. Run it: week 4 first alerts, the rule fires in week 5. Print one `#` per 0.05 of PSI, capped at 30.
lessons.ask: Why does the rule wait for two weeks in a row, and what does that cost?
lessons.learn: Read 16.3 steps 3, 5 and 6: the retrain rule as code, the text dashboard, and the runbook.

lessons.title: Runbook, tests, README, link to Project 12
lessons.build: Write the runbook (watch, alert, retrain). Add tests: identical data gives PSI near 0, bins come from the reference, the rule needs persistence. Write the README from the outline and push. Extension: call `psi()` every 100 requests in your Project 12 pipeline.
lessons.ask: Drift happened. Do you retrain right away? Say three steps.
lessons.learn: Read 16.3: acceptance criteria, pitfalls, three extensions, interview talking points and the README outline.

lessons.build: Closed book, 25 minutes: write everything you remember from the Math and Statistics cheat sheets (formulas, tests, pitfalls). Then open each appendix and mark every gap in red. Turn the 5 biggest gaps into flashcards.
lessons.ask: Without notes: state the p-value definition and the gradient of the logistic loss.
